implementationNote: Every leaf currently renders in its correct PRE-ANIMATION position with the right class name (`marketing-drift-leaf` / `marketing-scroll-leaf` / `marketing-responsive-leaf`), and the scroll-track wrapper is exposed via a React ref plus `data-scroll-track="hero"`. Nothing animates yet. The configs below are decoded from the original and are the authority for what the motion WILL be — they are not a claim that it ships working.

ui-default.usedBy: hamburger bars; the BadgeLink hover transition

viewportTrigger.note: NO delay and NO stagger anywhere. Card grids have no listing stagger.

scrollSpring.hook: useScroll({ target: heroScrollTrackRef, offset: ['start end', 'end start'] })
scrollSpring.drives: 6 scroll leaves, 2 scaleX line draws, 2 opacity reveals
scrollSpring.correction: The 'drives 6 scroll leaves' figure is Hero.jsx's own comment. The real HERO_LEAVES table is 4 drift + 8 scroll-tracked, which is what the raw measurement shows too (_reference/recon-b/partner_50pros.json motion[2..13]). src/lib/leaves.js:22-23 says '6 drift / 6 scroll' and is WRONG about its own data: entries 0,1,6,7 carry `from` (drift) and entries 2,3,4,5,8,9,10,11 carry `track` (scroll).

QUOTE_LEAVES.RULE: STATIC BY DESIGN: initial === animate, no class, no transform delta. A contract must FORBID animating these.

OUR_PURPOSE_WREATH.note: 2 desktop + 2 phone. Plain with REAL alt text and no inline transform — unlike every other leaf on the site. Never add a drift class.

reducedMotion.behaviour: transition-duration and animation-duration forced to 0.01ms; recognition lines forced to scaleX(1); hero hearts forced to opacity 1; scroll and drift leaves forced to their rotate-only resting transform.

absentPatterns: no smooth-scroll (html scroll-behavior is explicitly auto)
